records.quote: The FLEX (Flame Extinguishment Experiment) investigation aims to map the flammability limits of liquid fuels in microgravity environments, measure the effectiveness of various gaseous fire suppressants such as CO2, He, and SF6, and develop reliable predictive models for combustion limits under reduced gravity conditions.
records.derivation: Objective statement ('aims to'), not a statement that the tests were run in microgravity (brief rule 3). No g-level stated. 'reduced gravity conditions' in the same sentence refers to the predictive models; not read as partial gravity.

records.quote: FLEX (Flame Extinguishment Experiment) investigates the effectiveness of fire suppressants in microgravity and quantify the effect of different possible crew exploration atmospheres on fire suppression.
records.derivation: Scope sentence of the Description of Data: says what FLEX investigates, not that the tests were run in microgravity. No g-level stated. Grammar ('quantify') as in the source.

records.source_file: psi-data/PSI-69/Engineering Documents/PSI-69_Engineering Documents_FLEX Engineering Requirements Document.pdf
records.quote: The Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus is a mini-facility designed to support Principal Investigators (PI) interested in studying various aspects of droplet combustion in a microgravity environment.
records.derivation: Facility-purpose sentence about the MDCA, not about FLEX tests. Sentence spans three PDF lines, joined with one space. Two sentences later the same paragraph (section 3.1, printed page 4) says FLEX and FLEX-2 'have been selected for use in the MDCA', and the PSI record section=experimentHardware lists the MDCA for FLEX. The document itself is the FLEX-2 ERD (FLX-REQ-0001, February 04, 2010), filed in PSI-69 under the name 'FLEX Engineering Requirements Document'.

records.quote: The FLEX (Flame Extinguishment Experiment) investigation aims to map the flammability limits of liquid fuels in microgravity environments, measure the effectiveness of various gaseous fire suppressants such as CO2, He, and SF6, and develop reliable predictive models for combustion limits under reduced gravity conditions.
records.derivation: The sentence names the phase ('liquid fuels'). Same sentence as R1. Section=hypothesis also says 'liquid fuel droplets'.

PSI flight-program field. Nothing in the documents read places the FLEX burns on another vehicle; ERD page 12 says the MDCA goes into the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) 'onboard the International Space Station (ISS)'.

records.value: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)-Fluids and Combustion Facility (FCF)
records.value_original: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)-Fluids and Combustion Facility (FCF)
records.quote: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)-Fluids and Combustion Facility (FCF), Multi-user Droplet Combustion Appartatus (MDCA)
records.derivation: First item of the PSI hardware field. Shared with FLEX-2: the FLEX-2 ERD (page 12) places the MDCA, used by FLEX and FLEX-2, in the CIR of the FCF.

records.quote: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)-Fluids and Combustion Facility (FCF), Multi-user Droplet Combustion Appartatus (MDCA)
records.derivation: Second item of the PSI hardware field. 'Appartatus' is the source spelling (the ERD spells it 'Apparatus'); kept as written. Shared with FLEX-2: ERD page 12 says FLEX and FLEX-2 'have been selected for use in the MDCA'.

records.quote: Table 6: Quiescent environment LOI test matrix.
records.derivation: The caption states the configuration. The table header on the same page reads 'No fiber support, Flow: 0.0 cm/s' and lists Test No. 1-14 (C7H16) and 15-28 (CH3OH). Confidence lowered because page 5 says these matrices 'are designed to allow the engineering team to adequately plan for the experiment and do not represent the final test matrix': the Test No. are planned numbers, not confirmed as PSI experimental-table test ids.

records.quote: Table 7: Slow flow LOI test matrix
records.derivation: Caption has no final period. Header on the same page: 'SiC fiber support, Flow: 1.5 cm/s'; Test No. 29-39 (C7H16) and 40-50 (CH3OH). Page 5 says Tables 6 and 7 determine the LOI 'in quiescent and flowing environments, respectively'. None of the controlled terms (opposed, concurrent, coflow) is stated for this flow past a droplet; the term is kept as written. Planned matrix (page 5: 'do not represent the final test matrix').

Header of Table 8 (CO2 suppressant efficacy; table continues on page 9). The header spans two lines ('No fiber' / 'support'), joined with one space. Flow 0.0 cm/s read as quiescent: the caption does not use the word, but Table 6, captioned 'Quiescent environment', carries the same 'Flow: 0.0 cm/s'. Also a planned matrix (page 5), so the Test No. are not confirmed PSI test ids.

Header of Table 9 (He suppressant efficacy; table continues on page 11). The header spans two lines, joined with one space. Flow 0.0 cm/s read as quiescent (same convention as Table 6). Planned matrix (page 5).

Header of Table 10 (SF6 suppressant efficacy; table continues on page 13). The header spans two lines, joined with one space. Flow 0.0 cm/s read as quiescent (same convention as Table 6). Planned matrix (page 5).

records.quote: Table 11: Suppressant efficacy in a slow flow test matrix.
records.derivation: Header on the same page: 'No fiber, Flow: 1.5 cm/s' (CO2 suppressant); Test No. 219-238 (C7H16) and 239-258 (CH3OH). Page 5: 'The tests described in Table 11 examine how a slow, sub-buoyant flow influences the efficacy of a single suppressant'. No controlled term fits; kept as written. Planned matrix (page 5).

Header of Table 12 ('Suppressant in a radiative environment', CO2). The header spans two lines, joined with one space. Flow 0.0 cm/s read as quiescent (same convention as Table 6). Planned matrix (page 5).

records.quote: For the slow flow tests (in the flight experiment), the configuration of the flight hardware did not allow for adequate diagnostics over the entire test for a droplet in a uniform, steady convective flow.
records.derivation: Says slow-flow tests exist in the flight experiment but not which ones. The same paragraph says the flow is 'imparted by translating the droplet at a slow, uniform speed' and, in future tense, that 'a number of these tests will have droplets with a slow drift velocity'. This paragraph reproduces Test Plan section 5.3 (pages 4-5) with some verbs moved to past tense. No controlled term fits; kept as written. The record text never uses the word 'quiescent'.

records.quote: FLEX and the follow-on FLEX–2 experiments are exploiting the microgravity environment to study the spherically symmetric combustion of liquid droplets.
records.derivation: NASA ISS Researcher's Guide (2015), present-tense description of the FLEX experiments flown in the CIR; names FLEX and the microgravity environment.

records.quote: FLEX series of experiments showed for the first time that quasi-steady stable flames can be established surrounding a droplet in microgravity under certain conditions
records.derivation: Results sentence about the FLEX series in the CFI Science Final Report (a different investigation's document: SHARED_LINEAGE). Past tense, about what the FLEX experiments showed.

not_found.looked_in: Record text, all sections: none. DoD paragraphs 1-13: none. Test Plan, all 15 pages: page 4 (section 5.2.8) only requires chamber gas temperature measurement with 'accuracy shall be at least ± 0.5C', no value. ERD, all 37 pages: page 22 (4.1.37) 'FLEX-2 shall provide ambient temperature within the range of 18 – 27 °C.' and page 29 (4.1.97, measurement accuracy 'in the range of 18-27º C') are FLEX-2 requirements in the FLEX-2 ERD (FLX-REQ-0001) that PSI files under PSI-69. Not proposed for FLEX: that would fill the value by analogy with FLEX-2 (brief rule 7), and it is a design requirement ('shall'), not a measured condition. The auditor may decide otherwise.

not_found.variable: gravity_regime (sentence stating as a fact that the FLEX tests were run in microgravity)
not_found.looked_in: Record text, DoD, Test Plan pages 1-15, ERD pages 1-37. Only objective, scope or facility-purpose sentences were found (R1-R3). Not used: section=projectType 'Microgravity Investigation' (category label); section=hypothesis (a hypothesis); Test Plan page 1 document title 'Droplet Flame Extinguishment in Microgravity (FLEX)'; ERD page 24 (4.1.52 G-Level) acceleration limit, which is a FLEX-2 requirement. 'Flight experiment' (record section=approach; Test Plan page 4) says where the tests ran, not the gravity level. No partial-gravity statement anywhere; 'reduced gravity' (section=objective) refers to models.

not_found.variable: gravity_regime = normal_gravity (1-g comparison tests run by FLEX)
not_found.looked_in: Record text, DoD, Test Plan pages 1-15, ERD pages 1-37. None found. Test Plan page 4 ('based on ground-based testing'), page 5 ('extensive ground testing in the drop towers at the NASA Glenn Research Center') and footnote 7 ('the complimentary ground-based program') mention ground tests without a gravity level or test ids. The '1 − g' column of Table 2 (page 3) belongs to Takahashi et al. (2004) cup-burner results, not to FLEX.

not_found.variable: flow_configuration mapped to executed (PSI experimental-table) test ids
not_found.looked_in: Record text and DoD give no test ids for quiescent or slow-flow tests. The Test Plan gives only planned Test No. 1-290, and page 5 says the matrices 'do not represent the final test matrix'. R8-R14 carry the planned numbers with a 'Test Plan Table N' prefix so they cannot be joined by accident to PSI test ids.

lineage: The PSI-69 file named 'FLEX Engineering Requirements Document' is the FLEX-2 ERD (FLX-REQ-0001, Final, February 04, 2010; page 1). FLEX and FLEX-2 share the MDCA in the CIR/FCF: ERD page 12, 'Currently, the Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX) and the Flame Extinguishment Experiment 2 (FLEX-2) have been selected for use in the MDCA.' (the PDF breaks 'FLEX-' / '2)' across lines); page 9, 'FLEX-2 will use the existing Multi-User Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA) hardware and software platform already developed as a baseline for meeting many of the requirements found in this document.' The Test Plan (page 1) was 'extracted from the Research Requirements Document for Droplet Flame Extinguishment in Microgravity (FLEX) by FA Williams, M Hicks, V Nayagam, MY Choi, FL Dryer and BD Shaw and dated November 4, 2005'. Its printed page numbers (11-12, 44-55) suggest pages taken from that RRD. Record section=approach reproduces Test Plan section 5.3.
